newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 10.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* U.S. Rep. Bill Archer, R-Texas, outlined a plan to cut federal taxes.
* Cable stocks rose after several deals valued at more than $4 billion, including a $1 billion investment by Microsoft Corp, offered hope for the embattled industry.
* Chrysler Corp is expected to announce a plan to equip more than a third of its future minivans to run on ethanol and gasoline.
* BankAmerica Corp has agreed to sell its consumer-finance unit for $1.6 billion to Travelers Group Inc .
* Atlas Copco AB has agreed to acquire Prime Service for $1.2 billion.
* PepsiCo Inc named Andrall Pearson, a former president of the firm, chairman and chief executive of its restaurant unit, which is to be spun off later this year.
* The dollar fell against the mark and yen amid concerns that France may seek to block Europe's move toward a single currency.
* The Dow Jones Industrials average rose 42.72 points to 7478.50, a new record level.
* Frontier Corp is expected to name Joseph Clayton as president and heir apparent to Chairman and Chief Executive Ronald Bittner, who in January underwent emergency surgery to remove a brain tumour.
* IBM is looking to close World Avenue, a "virtual" shopping mall the company opened a year ago.
* Armstrong World Industries Inc launched a $354 million hostile bid for Domco Inc.
* German television station Puls-TV has begun bankruptcy proceedings.
* Fisher Scientific International Inc has adopted a shareholder-rights plan, a move that could thwart a takeover attempt by its largest shareholder.
* Coffee futures rose amid reports of a possible frost in Brazil.

* Heard on the Street: Tickets to one of Wall Street's hottest takeover parties just got a little pricier. Yesterday, BankAmerica Corp said it agreed, as expected, to acquire Robertson, Stephens & Co, a closely held investment banking boutique, for $540 million -- or an astonishing five times book value, or assets minus liabilities.
* Credit Markets: Bond prices fell yesterday in what many traders said was a "healthy" correction after a sharp rally Friday on technical factors.
